question: Can purpose-aware pressure-head node placement recover 50-100 row fidelity with only 25-40 generated table rows, without changing interpolation, solver policy or physical semantics?
motivation: P1 showed a sharp fidelity loss between 50 and 25 rows while 50 rows remained highly accurate, suggesting placement rather than row count alone limits the sparse representation.

hypotheses.H3a: Redistributing sparse rows toward high-curvature constitutive regions reduces Richards error at fixed row count.
hypotheses.H3b: A 25-40 row purpose-aware grid can approach the fidelity of the naive 50-100 row log grid.
hypotheses.H3c: Purpose-aware placement retains the runtime advantage of sparse tables.

placement_rule.authority_sampling: dense analytical default-MvG sampling over the same dry-to-kbranch head domain
placement_rule.importance: combined normalized curvature/variation score from theta and log(K), with endpoint preservation
placement_rule.no_case_calibration: weights and algorithm are fixed before candidate results are inspected

fixed: same wet continuation and saturation handling
decision: Compare C25/C32/C40 with L25/L50 and prior L100. Identify Pareto-nondominated candidates without selecting a winner in advance.
